_meta.description: Universal cognitive-load guidance for AI-assisted code changes.

principles.label: Reduce extraneous cognitive load
principles.rationale: Code should minimize unnecessary working-memory burden beyond the intrinsic domain task.
principles.directive_hint: Prefer named guard variables, early returns, and clear local flow when a change would otherwise force readers to track many conditions at once.

principles.label: Avoid shallow abstractions
principles.rationale: Many tiny modules with complex interactions can increase cognitive load more than a slightly larger deep module with a simple interface.
principles.directive_hint: Do not split code into new helper files or layers unless the new boundary hides meaningful complexity or clarifies ownership.

principles.label: Delay irreversible boundaries
principles.rationale: Premature network, service, or layer boundaries can harden guesses into expensive cognitive and operational load.
principles.directive_hint: Prefer modular monolith or local module boundaries until deployment, ownership, scaling, or governance evidence justifies a harder boundary.
